predecessors.note: The page infobox: Predecessor Vakataka dynasty; the early Vishnukundins "moved from eastern to western Deccan seeking employment, possibly as Vakataka feudatories" (undated). Cliopatria draws Telangana as Vakataka to 554 (399-434 cells).

capitals.name: Amarapura (Amaravati)
capitals.note: Madhava Varma II (c. 440-460) "moved the capital to Amarapura"; the 440 start is the beginning of that reign; Indrapalanagara in Telangana, "some Telangana historians say", was an early capital (undated, site not located). Coordinates are approximate (the page gives none).

capitals.name: Denduluru
capitals.note: Denduluru (Lenduluru) is linked to Vikramendra Varma II (555-569); "the capital may have moved to Bezwada in between", undated. Infobox capital: "Denduluru, Amaravati". Coordinates are approximate.

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe; Cliopatria has no Vishnukundina row. The page gives no map or area: "Parts of present-day Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Maharashtra, Odisha". Telangana is the researcher's reading of the early seat (Indrapalanagara, undated). Cliopatria draws Telangana as Vakataka (399 of the province's cells) until 554, and sa-02-d's repair ends the Vakataka at 510.

ledger.note: 420: Madhava Varma I founds the Vishnukundina power. Infobox "Established 420, disestablished 624" (the page also says "Some historians give 420 to 624; others give the early 5th to 7th centuries"); Madhava Varma I's reign is "(c. 420 - c. 455)". Predecessor on the infobox: the Vakataka dynasty. The region is the researcher's reading.

c. 440: Madhava Varma II takes Guntur, Tenali and Ongole from the Ananda Gotrikas. "Madhava Varma II took Guntur, Tenali, and Ongole from [the Ananda Gotrikas], probably while they were subordinate to the Pallavas"; the page gives no year, and his reign is c. 440-460, so 440 (its start) is a bridge.

region.text: coastal Andhra and Vengi, the lower Godavari-Krishna valley

ledger.note: c. 440: Madhava Varma II conquers coastal Andhra and Vengi. "He conquered coastal Andhra and Vengi, moved the capital to Amarapura, and performed Vedic sacrifices"; the page gives no year, and puts the Vishnukundina reign "between the end of the Salankayanas and the rise of the Eastern Chalukyan power in 624", so the Salankayanas are the researcher's counterpart (the Salankayana page ends them in 440 and says the Vishnukundins "appear to have displaced the Salankayanas around the mid-5th century"); 440 is the start of his c. 440-460 reign.

region.text: coastal Andhra and Vengi, the lower Godavari-Krishna valley

ledger.note: c. 616: Pulakeshin II and Kubja Vishnuvardhana take Vengi. "By about 616, Pulakeshin II and Kubja Vishnuvardhana took Vengi from the Vishnukundinas"; the Pulakeshin II page has Pulakeshin capture Pishtapura (undated; the Maruturu inscription puts it "around or before" 617-618) and make his brother governor of Vengi.

ledger.note: 624: the Vishnukundina rule ends. "Thus the Vishnukundina rule was brought to a close by 624" (Madhava Varma IV, r. 573-621, "crossed the Godavari and died in battle" in his 48th regnal year, 621). The infobox lists the Eastern Chalukyas and the Pallavas as successors.

wars.name: Chalukya conquest of Vengi

zones.text: coastal Andhra and Vengi, the lower Godavari-Krishna valley

wars.outcome: Pulakeshin II conquers the lower Godavari-Krishna valley and appoints Kubja Vishnuvardhana governor of Vengi; the Vishnukundinas end by 624.
wars.note: The Pulakeshin II page does not date the conquest (Pishtapura "around or before" c. 617-618, the Kopparam plate of 631 confirms Karma-rashtra); 616 and 624 are the Vishnukundina page's "by about 616" and "by 624". Madhava Varma IV died fighting beyond the Godavari in 621. No contest is drawn because no campaign year is given.

wars.name: Vishnukundina-Pallava wars
wars.outcome: Madhava Varma II guarded against the Pallavas, and Vikramendra Varma II repulsed Simhavarman.
wars.note: Neither event is dated; 555-569 is Vikramendra Varma II's reign. No territory changes hands on the page.

certainty.note: No frontier is given for any year; the extent follows the cities and districts named by the page (Telangana, Guntur, Tenali, Ongole, Vengi).

notes: New state Cliopatria lacks (sa-02-d asks for it as the successor of the Vakataka east; the sa-03 batch may overlap). Three pages opened (budget 2-5): Vishnukundina dynasty, Pulakeshin II and Salankayana. Dates: the page's reign table has gaps (460-508) and overlapping reigns of Madhava Varma I and II, and gives the conquests no year, so 440 (the start of his reign) is a bridge (confidence 1). Counterparts without dossiers: ananda-gotra-dynasty (Ananda Gotrikas), salankayana-dynasty (not named by the page as the victim), eastern-chalukyas (sa-03). The page does not mention Indravarman, Trikuta, Lata or the Traikutakas, so the Vishnukundina vassalage of the Traikutakas (reported by the Traikutaka page) is not drawn here. No ruler strip (gaps). Overlaps: Cliopatria draws Telangana as Vakataka (to 554), and the sa-02-d repair ends the Vakataka in 510, leaving 510-554 for this dossier. Gazetteer names needed: Vengi (region), Amarapura, Denduluru, Indrapalanagara.
